recent_posts.title: PostgreSQL Hybrid Search Using pgvector and Cohere
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the implementation of a hybrid search engine using Cohere and pgvector on PostgreSQL. It explains the benefits of combining keyword and semantic search for better search results. The post also provides code examples for setup, data insertion, keyword search, semantic search, and reranking. It concludes with an example of using the hybrid search in a retrieval augmented generation (RAG) application.

recent_posts.title: PostgreSQL Data Cleaning vs. Python Data Cleaning
recent_posts.summary: This post explores how PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB can be used for efficient data cleaning tasks, replacing the need for tools like Excel, R, or Python. By cleaning data directly within the database, tasks can be performed more efficiently, saving time in the long run.

recent_posts.title: Building a Copilot for Git History With pgvector & Timescale
recent_posts.summary: OpenSauced uses Timescale to provide insights and metrics on open-source projects at GitHub's massive scale. They chose Timescale for its promising performance, familiarity with PostgreSQL, and cost-effectiveness. They ingest GitHub events through the events firehose and use Timescale's time-series mechanisms for deep insights and metrics. They also use pgvector to perform fast similarity search on vector embeddings, enhancing their AI-powered capabilities.

recent_posts.title: What We’re Excited About PostgreSQL 17
recent_posts.summary: PostgreSQL 17 is an upcoming release with significant changes to modernize the database. It includes features like pg_createsubscriber, support for merge and split partitions, incremental file system backup, failover of logical slots, and reporting of optimizer memory usage in EXPLAIN command. Timescale has made several contributions to PostgreSQL 17. The release is aimed at enhancing performance, scalability, security, and compatibility.

recent_posts.title: Powering Real-Time Transit Analytics From a 1 TB Table
recent_posts.summary: Hopthru utilizes Timescale to power real-time transit analytics from a 1 TB table. They collect and analyze automated passenger counting (APC) data from transit agencies to help improve public transportation. With Hopthru's analysis suite, agencies can optimize their routes and network based on ridership data. They make use of TimescaleDB's performance capabilities and features like hypertables and continuous aggregates. Hopthru's future roadmap includes building a product called Hopthru Cleanse to improve data accuracy and help agencies achieve NTD certification.

recent_posts.title: How to Collapse Your Stack Using PostgreSQL for Everything
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the concept of collapsing your stack by using PostgreSQL for multiple use cases. It highlights the challenges of stack sprawl with multiple databases and emphasizes the benefits of simplicity and using PostgreSQL for various workload types.

recent_posts.title: Ingesting 1M Inserts per Minute to Help Save Devs’ Resources
recent_posts.summary: Judoscale helps engineering teams manage server resources by automatically scaling resources based on traffic metrics. They use Timescale for data retention and aggregation, and D3 for data visualization. Judoscale ingests a million inserts per minute and primarily uses Ruby for their system.

recent_posts.title: 13 Tips to Improve PostgreSQL Database Insert Performance
recent_posts.summary: This post provides 13 tips to improve PostgreSQL database insert performance, including using indexes in moderation, reconsidering foreign key constraints, avoiding unnecessary unique keys, using separate disks for WAL and data, and using performant disks. It also suggests using TimescaleDB to improve ingest performance and provides additional techniques for optimizing insert performance with TimescaleDB. The post emphasizes the importance of insert performance in real-time or high-volume databases and highlights the value of time-series data and application monitoring. It also provides resources for further learning and optimization of PostgreSQL performance.

recent_posts.title: How Timescale Replication Works: Enabling HA in PostgreSQL
recent_posts.summary: Timescale has released early access to database replication, enabling high availability and fault tolerance. Replicas in Timescale act as duplicates of the main database and can be used to scale read workloads and isolate the primary database for writes. Users can direct read queries to replicas for improved performance. Timescale automates the setup and management of replicas, making it easy to increase data availability.

recent_posts.title: Time-Series Forecasting With TimescaleDB and Prophet
recent_posts.summary: Learn about the importance of time-series forecasting and how to use TimescaleDB and Prophet for efficient data analysis. Explore the scalability and data retention policies of TimescaleDB, and the automatic detection of trends and seasonality with Prophet. Discover how to install and set up the database, insert time-series data, and model using Prophet. Find answers to frequently asked questions and learn about the potential of integrating TimescaleDB and Prophet for data-driven decision-making.
